filename: Inland migration of near-surface crevasses in the Amundsen Sea Sector, West Antarctica.pdf
title: Inland migration of near-surface crevasses in the Amundsen Sea Sector, West Antarctica
code_availability: Scripts for creating figures and crevasse propagation rate data products are available at https://github.com/hoffmaao/thwaites_crevasses. Image masking software is available at https://github.com/hoffmaao/EarthMasker.
testbed_rationale: The study develops an image segmentation computer vision model (U-Net) to map surface crevasses from SAR imagery and develops an analytical firn tensile strength model; it does not provide an ML parameterization or surrogate model for climate/Earth system models.
pain_points: SAR imagery detects features differently depending on satellite look angle, surface slope, and crevasse orientation.
Surface melt events and temperature anomalies alter surface radar backscatter, creating false positive outliers in crevasse area tracking.
Lack of translational equivariance in CNNs requires custom tiling, padding (20 px), and clipping schemes to avoid boundary artifacts.
Snow bridges obscure crevasses in optical imagery, and radar penetration limits exact measurement of crevasse depth.
extraction_notes: The paper uses deep learning strictly for satellite remote-sensing computer vision (semantic segmentation of SAR imagery), coupled with classical glaciological stress calculations and a geometric firn mechanics model.
